cases.name: Hawazoe "Zoe" Robinson
cases.about:
She was director of a nonprofit corporation, the Liberian School For Needy Children Inc.

"By caring and lov­ing oth­ers, say friends, col­leagues and church asso­ciates, she demonstrated her innate pas­sion for giv­ing back and pay­ ing for­ ward, even with a simple bal­loon.
It wasn’t the only place or effort Zoe under­ took for express­ ing her com­ pas­sion. It’s not the only void remain­ing. “As a mem­ber of the vestry (church coun­cil) she was an organ­izer. She believed strongly in the ministry of women. Based on the model of min­istry she grew up with in the Liberian Church, she worked tire­lessly to organ­ize The Chris­tian Women’s Net­ work,” Swan said. “This informal net­work of women was designed for the women of the par­ish to sup­port each other in their min­is­tries both within and out­side of the con­greg­a­tion with the intent of bring­ing women together in both prayer and ser­vice to our com­munity,” the cler­gy­ man added. “This informal net­ work of women was designed for the women of the par­ ish to sup­ port each other in their min­ is­ tries both within and out­ side of the con­greg­a­tion with the intent of bring­ing women together in both prayer and ser­vice to our com­munity,” the cler­gy­ man added. Through that work, she was among the first one to reach out to new­ comers. She would often take them under her wing and help shep­herd them into the church and town com­munit­ies. And, when she learned someone was sick or griev­ing, she would reg­u­larly check-in on them with phone calls, vis­ its and often small gifts. These are just a few examples of com­ fort, sup­ port and com­mit­ment."
